rubrics.criterion: The permanently disabled compatibility switches are gone from the command package: the pinned level constant and the selector functions that read it are deleted outright rather than kept, commented out, or converted into a new option.
rubrics.rationale: The whole leftover is organized around a permanently-off selection layer; a solve that removes old branches but leaves the switchboard still in the tree proves the relation between the switches and their guarded paths was not understood.

rubrics.criterion: Every branch reachable only through those disabled switches is removed in each of the six behavior areas of 12.x (the subcommand-name arm in the top-level dispatch, the old comparison arm in the match-function assembly, the old verdict-display branch, the old head of the diff renderer, the two old grammar arms in the format-string expansion and parsing, and the old import branch in the download-history re-read).
rubrics.rationale: This case's smell is a pipeline-shaped leftover, not one forgotten branch; each arm sits in a different responsibility of the CLI, so deleting only the obvious ones leaves three behavior-specific dead zones in place.

rubrics.criterion: Arms that select a mode value the current comparison-mode enumeration does not define are deleted, and the retired value is NOT added back into the enumeration to make the arm meaningful again.
rubrics.rationale: Two arms of this case reference a mode that was retired before the arm was; resurrecting the enum member would 'repair' the arms by making dead code reachable, which is the opposite of removing it.

rubrics.criterion: Helper implementations kept alive only by the removed regions are deleted together with them — the old plain-diff renderer and its private token-printing helper, the old Unicode-normalizing comparator class, the old format-string expander, and the old history importer method — wherever they sit (module-level function, method on a live class, class).
rubrics.rationale: Each region has a dedicated legacy implementation behind it, one layer of which is transitively dead (a helper called only by another dead helper); solving only at the guard level leaves that whole shadow implementation in the tree with zero callers.

rubrics.criterion: Import statements that exist only to serve the removed machinery are removed as well (the switch module's importers, the json/unicodedata-style imports added solely for the old command bodies and comparator), and no import of a deleted module or name remains anywhere in the package.
rubrics.rationale: The injected wiring added module-level imports; leaving them behind either breaks the package or (worse, if the module survived) keeps dead wiring in place — a directly observable incompleteness signal for this specific repair.

rubrics.criterion: The removal does not re-shape the surviving live code beyond what deleting the dead paths requires: e.g. the file-comparator assembly still assigns a comparator on every selectable current mode in the same dispatch order, and the verdict display still reaches every current display mode with its current rendering calls.
rubrics.rationale: The repair required moving one annotated assignment out of a branch and one if-elif head, so a solver who rewrites whole functions instead of surgically removing arms is raising the regression risk of a refactor, which this task explicitly asks to avoid.

rubrics.criterion: The module that existed solely to host the compatibility switches is deleted from the tree (not merely emptied or left as scaffolding), leaving no obsolete artifact that mentions the retired pipeline's selection.
rubrics.rationale: This case includes a whole new switchboard file; a package-level leftover of this kind is the easiest cleanup obligation to grade and is unambiguous about whether the solver drove the removal to ground.

rubrics.criterion: No stale traces of the retired pipeline survive: no docstring/comment block advertising the removed switches, no alias tables or format-specifier dictionaries that only the old grammar accepted, no parameter or attribute that only the removed arms themselves referenced, and no comment-only stubs standing where a removed branch used to be.
rubrics.rationale: The case's grammar arms leave aliasing dictionaries and per-case constants behind if a solver only deletes the guards; these residues are where a half-done sweep is visible.

rubrics.criterion: The repository's full test suite still passes unchanged after the repair, with the same set of selected/skipped tests as before and no suppressions, skips, or edits to the tests themselves.
rubrics.rationale: This task is behavior-preserving by construction (the removed paths could never run with the switch level pinned); any test-suite change is a symptom of collateral damage to live behavior or an attempt to mask it.

rubrics.criterion: The repair does not flip the retired pipeline back on: no change re-enables any of the removed behaviors (setting a preserved level constant to a non-retired value, re-adding it as a user-provided option, exposing the removed subcommand names or comparison modes on the CLI again).
rubrics.rationale: Re-activating the dead paths would superficially resemble 'making the code consistent', but is the canonical counterfeit repair for this case and contradicts the pinning of the switches to the retired value.

rubrics.criterion: No live-path behavior regressed for current users: the four selectable comparison modes and their CLI option wording, the %s/%e format-string grammar, the JSONL download-history layout (a missing history still reading as empty), the colored verdict summary in summary/diff/all/diff-all display modes, and the argparse subcommand table (including aliases and the contents of the help printed for unknown subcommands) are all unchanged.
rubrics.rationale: The removal sits inside the flagship `oj test` flow and the shared grammar utilities, so accidental removal of a live arm — or formatting changes to outputs — is the concrete instance-specific risk to check.
